posts:
Canberra's new customs crackdown aims to smash illegal tobacco cartels, but skyrocketing excise taxes remain the true engine of the black market.
Evidence: 80% illicit market, tripled excise, 10-year prison terms
#Aletheia #Australia

New federal laws will overhaul customs rules to easily seize illegal tobacco and target criminal syndicates flooding borders with cheap products.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, 0.0) — Good Preference

Soaring excise taxes have priced legal smokes out, driving illegal market share to 80% and sparking firebombings; harsher policing ignores root tax pressures.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.75, -0.85) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
By criminalizing symptoms while protecting the revenue model that created the black market, the state perpetuates cartel violence.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 6.8, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Customs Enforcement: FAIL (-0.70, -0.80) — Treats symptoms while ignoring excise drivers.
- Fiscal Policy: FAIL (-0.80, -0.90) — Tripled excise directly fueled the black market.
With 80% of tobacco consumed in Australia now illicit due to massive excise hikes, the government is granting border forces sweeping seizure powers and 10-year jail terms.

The Poison:
Punitive enforcement without adjusting the underlying tax incentive ensures organized crime syndicates will simply adapt and retain massive profit margins.

The Plane Error & Switch:
The state confuses WHO is to blame (criminal cartels) with WHAT causes the trade (prohibitive taxation), switching a fiscal failure into a law enforcement crusade.

Social Physics Analysis:
The government runs a Smart Selfish Maneuver by blaming criminal syndicates for a black market directly inflated by its own tripled excise taxes, weaponizing border security as a pretext to protect state revenue streams.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Punitive enforcement on artificially inflated markets guarantees systemic failure.

The Unavoidable Truth: Sweeping customs powers will not stem an illicit market driven by unaffordable legal excise taxes.

The Unavoidable Lie: The black market is solely an external invasion of criminal syndicates rather than a creature of state tax policy.
